Some libraries may encode data before dropping them into a cookie, so the limit is not the size of the raw data but sometime the size of the *encoded* data.

The JWT part confuses me a lot because we are talking about cookies and cookie limits, what does JWT have to do with this? If you put data into a JWT then the size limits of a cookie do not apply.

Now if are putting a JWT _into_ a cookie as _cookie parameter_, then what matters is the *total size of the encoded JWT* and not "part of a JWT".

And I shared my little simple-stupid snippet to prove your script to be wrong.

You can count that I have went through all related RFC's and pointing to those does not give any extra value. Especially, cookies are this kind of piece of technology, where reality and specs are not always walk hand-in-hand.

But to make you more entertained:
* https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-httpbis-rfc6265bis#name-the-set-cookie-header-field
> If the sum of the lengths of the name string and the value string is more than 4096 octets, abort these steps and ignore the set-cookie-string entirely.

> Did I understand correctly?

By principle yes.

> Overly large cookies might be ignored by the browser and not sent with requests.

Technically this is not precise, proposed version may me interpreted as "browser stores the cookie but just do not send it", but the reality is that browser ignores the set-cookie header field (or the command browser cookie API alternative).

I'm not sure that so long text is required for that requirement. I think this is enough:

> otherwise the cookie is ignored by the user-agent.

Shorter and more exact?

"_Verify that when the application writes a cookie the cookie name and value length combined are not over 4096 bytes. Overly large cookies will not be stored by the browser and therefore not sent with requests, preventing the user form accessing the session mechanism._"

(If I thought the shorter version was clear enough, I wouldn't be arguing this :) )

"_Verify that when the application writes a cookie the cookie name and value length combined are not over 4096 bytes. Overly large cookies will not be stored by the browser and therefore not sent with requests, preventing the user from using application functionality which requires that cookie._"

I think I meant:

"_Verify that when the application writes a cookie the cookie name and value length combined are not over 4096 bytes. Overly large cookies will not be stored by the browser and therefore not sent with requests, preventing the user from using application functionality which requires that cookue._"
